text:
Asha P.: quick note — after the storage-telemetry run I correlated p99 spikes with a flurry of tiny offloads (~4-32B pages) from hybrid pools. This looks different from earlier fragmentation spikes; it's IO amplification on NVMe (lots of small writes, high queue depth).

Diego: saw the graphs. nvme IOPS went through the roof while bandwidth stayed moderate, latency ballooned. root cause seems many small write syscalls rather than consolidated IO.

Nina: is this the same as the coalesce-missed-path we've talked about? or are we seeing allocator churn creating lots of tiny offload ops?

Asha P.: allocator churn is part of it — ephemeral allocations + demote-on-idle currently trigger offload per slab-run. proposal: insert a transient coalescer layer in the offload path that buffers small pages for up to X ms or until N pages accumulate, then emit a single batched IO. tradeoffs: slightly longer time before eviction completes vs huge reduction in IOPS.

Diego: +1 on coalescer. addition: we should pair it with a per-tenant IO shaper (token-bucket) so a noisy tenant doesn't saturate the pool NVMe queue. This lets us maintain tail SLAs for other tenants.

Priya: how about admission at two levels: pool-global coalescer + tenant-level shaper. coalescer reduces syscalls; shaper smooths bursts. Also need to ensure we don't block critical reclaimers for out-of-memory.

Nina: implementation sketch:
```
coalescer:
  max_hold_ms: 6
  max_batch_pages: 64
  max_batch_bytes: 65536
shaper:
  bucket_rate_iops: 4000
  bucket_size_iops: 2000
  tenant_override: false
```
Coalescer would be best-effort: if a page must be offloaded synchronously for memory safety, bypass the buffer.

Asha P.: good. for correctness: synchronous safety path must still allow forced flushes. Also add a heuristic to prefer coalescing pages that share contiguous backing to reduce scatter IO.

Diego: perf concern: coalescer requires temporary CPU + memory to buffer pages. but we can use a ring-buffer pooled per-NUMA node to avoid allocations and copy costs. benchmark cost vs benefit in canary.

Priya: observability needs: coalesce_flush_count, coalesce_hold_ms_histogram, tenant_shaper_rejects, tenant_shaper_delay_ms, nvme_queue_depth_tagged. add tags: pool_id, tenant_id, numa_zone.

Nina: also add a debug knob to force single-page flushes for repro. makes it easier to validate correctness during canary.

Asha P.: rollback criteria for canary: if nvme avg queue depth increases >10% or p99 latency worsens >5% for the canary pool, revert. otherwise validate p50/p95/p99 improvements and token throughput.

Diego: timeline: I'll prototype coalescer + ring buffer this week. Nina will wire shaper and metrics. Priya will own canary run and rollback automation with devops.

devops-bot: canary job created: coalesce-shaper-canary-2026-04-01 03:30 UTC — job id 98765. Auto-rollback hook enabled.

Asha P.: excellent. one more long-term thought: we should fold coalescer hints into the allocator so the allocator can present coalescing-friendly layouts (prefetch-friendly grouping). That requires allocator refactor but could further reduce scatter. add to roadmap.

Priya: noted — I'll add a follow-up RFC ticket for allocator-layout hints (RFC-allocator-coalesce-2026).

Diego: capturing config and metrics in the PR. I'll post the draft link here when ready.

Nina: I'll prepare a tiny synthetic that reproduces the IO amplification to test locally.

Asha P.: thanks all. end here — follow-up in PR and canary results thread. :white_check_mark:
